value.author: samMularczyk
value.layerInfo: Colour fields marbled by layered swirls.

shape: The base field the swirl acts on. It is nearly constant across the frame at this scale, so almost everything visible is generated BY the swirl rather than being this pattern bent - Checks and Stripes differ more in character than in shape.
shapeScale: Frequency of the base field. On Edge it inverts: 1 is a tight edge, 0 a very wide gradient.
proportion: Shifts the field toward one end of the colour ramp, so one colour takes more of the frame.
softness: 0 gives hard banded edges between colours, 1 a raw linear ramp. Anything between quantises the ramp and then softens each step.
distortion: A noise warp applied BEFORE the swirl - it seeds it. Direction comes from one noise field and magnitude from a second.
swirl: Strength of each swirl pass. Amplitude falls as one over the iteration number, a harmonic series.
swirlIterations: How many swirl passes run. Because the amplitudes are harmonic this increases the warp's STRENGTH as well as its detail, roughly as the log of the count. Note it breaks before the last one, matching upstream: 10 runs nine passes.
scale: Zoom. Larger values pull the field in.
rotation: Rotates the whole field, in degrees.
colorCount: How many stops of the ramp are used.
evolution: Drives everything that moves, in degrees. Keyframe it, or drive it with a Frame behaviour - the rate is yours rather than tied to the comp clock.
loop: Makes the field return exactly to its start, so it can be cycled with no visible seam.
cycles: How many full revolutions of Evolution before it repeats. At 2 the field comes home at Evolution 720, not 360 - so a higher count travels further through the noise and gives more variation before the repeat.
